correctness.rationale: Let KG(n,2) have two-subsets as graph vertices and adjacency disjointness. Its two-independence complex X=Ind_2 has induced graph degree<=1. Any nonordinary face contains a disjoint pair e,f, which forces every remaining two-subset to meet both and hence lie in the same four-ground-element set T. Thus X=Y∪⋃_{|T|=4}D_T where Y=Ind_1 and D_T a simplex on six 2-subsets; D_T∩Y is the octahedral sphere S0*S0*S0 ≃ S2, and intersections of distinct D_T lie inside Y. The union A of closed stars of {1,i} in Y is contractible by its simplex nerve; Y\A consists of triangles on ground triples avoiding 1. Adjoining D_T for T containing 1 along disk portions of their S2 boundary builds a contractible X0 containing Y; quotient by X0 yields one S3 for each T⊂{2,…,n}, |T|=4, hence X≃wedge^{binom(n-1,4)} S3, including the n4 contractible case. The pair LES gives H3(X,Y)≅wedge^4 Z^n with induced orientation signs; oriented octahedral triangles yield connecting map δ=π∘ι_ε to H2(Y)≅wedge^3 Z^{n-1}. The integral splitting Z^n=Ze1⊕ker ε shows ker δ=wedge^4 ker ε, a natural integral S_n-module. Independently enumerated n=4,5,6 faces (64,261,747 augmented) and Euler −binom(n-1,4); checked sample permutations including identity (n6 trace5), transposition (−3), and 6-cycle (+1), consistent with fourth augmentation exterior power. Source checker covers n4..8 and all S5/S6 characters; finite cases are corroboration, not proof of all n or integral module statement.

value.rationale: Motivated uniform integral homotopy type and full S_n integral representation for a canonical nonchordal graph family at the first nonordinary higher-independence cutoff. The exterior fourth power of the augmentation lattice is a structural natural invariant, not a fixed-character table or a relabeling of ordinary independence. It includes but does not claim novelty for the known Petersen n5 case.

limitations: n>=4, two-subset KG(n,2), component cutoff exactly 2; the wedge equivalence is nonequivariant while H3 is integral equivariant.
